subject: Reserved commitment: pricing floor / pass-through proposal and exec approval path
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@atlashealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: 18mo reserved proposal + concern about GPU market volatility

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has sketched a baseline reserved ask: 18 months, 400 A100-equivalent GPU units (rolling monthly allocation), with a desire for a fixed unit price to simplify budgeting. I attached our stub commit schedule for reference (atlas_proposed_commit_schedule.xlsx).

Two things to flag from our side:
- We understand market pricing for GPUs is volatile; we need a protection that prevents us from being fully exposed if costs spike mid-tenor.
- Conversely, we also want a guarantee that if Redwood benefits from downward market moves you’ll pass some savings to Atlas.

Can Redwood propose contract language that balances those two objectives? Procurement would be comfortable with a mechanism that ties price adjustments to a transparent market index or vendor list (e.g., NVIDIA list / spot premium) and includes a cap on pass-through over the term.

Timing: we’re aiming to close commercial terms and get legal redlines by the week of Dec 6. Please let me know what options you can provide and whether you need info from NVIDIA (we can introduce your team).

Best,
Alice Monroe
Director, Strategic Procurement
Atlas Health

Attachment: atlas_proposed_commit_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: 18mo reserved proposal + concern about GPU market volatility

Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask and the schedule. Appreciate you calling out both upside and downside protections; we can absolutely propose options that trade predictability for some market linkage.

High-level options (attached as a short PDF for redlines): commit_pricing_options.pdf

Option A — Fixed unit price with limited market pass-through: Redwood offers a fixed baseline unit price for the 18-month term. If a validated market index (NVIDIA list or agreed reseller index) increases by more than 15% vs. the baseline quarter, Redwood reserves the right to pass-through up to 50% of the incremental GPU cost to Atlas, subject to a 12% per-term ceiling overall. Requires quarterly reconciliation and a 30-day notice window.

Option B — Indexed floor with rebate: Price is indexed to an agreed band. If market price drops below floor, Redwood passes through 50% of the saving as a rebate applied to the next billing cycle. If market price rises above ceiling, Redwood absorbs first 10% of the increase, pass-through thereafter up to a 20% cap absent executive approval.

Operational notes: both options include a SKU-level mapping (A100 v7 -> Redwood SKUs) and a commitment schedule that allows monthly reallocation within the 400-unit pool. Also propose an automatic NPI (new-product introduction) swap policy for equivalent hardware if vendor EOLs occur.

What I need from you: confirm whether Atlas prefers a fixed baseline or indexed approach, and whether you want the pass-through floor to tie to NVIDIA list price or an agreed reseller index. Once you confirm, we’ll route internally for finance/legal approval and come back with exact wording and an approval matrix.

Next steps: I’ll kick off a sensitivity analysis internally and loop Ben (sales ops) and Karthik (finance) to confirm thresholds for approval. If you’re open, we’d also like an intro to your NVIDIA account rep so we can get vendor confirmation on list/partner pricing behavior.

Thanks — speak soon.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: commit_pricing_options.pdf (summary of A/B options)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved commitment — sensitivity scenarios (internal)

Team —

Quick note after running the commit numbers against several GPU cost scenarios. I attached sensitivity_calc.csv with the modeling. Key takeaways:

- Baseline (vendor list flat): 400-unit commit at 18 months yields ~28% revenue uplift vs. on-demand and gives us good utilization smoothing.
- Market +20% vendor list: If we absorb increases beyond 10%, our margin on the deal drops below target; we need explicit cost pass-through to prevent >8% margin erosion.
- Market +35% vendor list: Without a floor/ceiling mechanism we’d be negative on contribution at current discounting levels.

Asks for approvals / gating rules:
1) Pricing team (Karthik) needs authority to sign up to a 12% absolute pass-through cap without Exec sign-off. Anything allowing >12% incremental pass-through of vendor increases should go to Sales leadership (Marissa) for approval.
2) Legal (Neha) to confirm if the quarterly reconciliation + 30-day notice is acceptable or whether procurement will push for more frequent reporting (we should hold to quarterly).
3) Sales (Monica/Ben) to get Atlas to accept vendor index definition and allow Redwood to provide reconciliation reports to Atlas (transparent feed).

I recommend Option A with a 15% trigger and 50% pass-through up to a 12% cap. It balances predictability for Atlas while protecting Redwood economics. Will defer to Karthik on the exact % mix.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sensitivity_calc.csv (model outputs)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved commitment — sensitivity scenarios (decision and next steps)

Team —

Reviewed Ben's modeling and legal constraints. Recommendation for the Atlas deal (to send to procurement):

- Adopt Option A (fixed baseline with market-triggered pass-through).
- Technical trigger: NVIDIA list price (or agreed reseller published index) > baseline quarter + 15% triggers reconciliation.
- Pass-through mechanics: Redwood may pass-through up to 50% of incremental GPU cost above the 15% trigger, but absolute pass-through applied to Atlas billing capped at 12% of baseline unit price over the full term.
- Internal approval matrix: Finance OKs up to 12% pass-through; anything that would increase customer bill by more than 12% requires Marissa Cole (SVP, Sales) written approval.
- Reconciliation cadence: quarterly; Atlas receives a reconciliation report with vendor price evidence. 30-day notice required before the first adjusted billing cycle.

Operational next steps:
1) Monica: share final choice with Atlas (Option A + NVIDIA index) and request intro to Atlas' NVIDIA rep.
2) Neha: prepare redline for SOW contract with the pricing tables and reconciliation appendix (use approval_matrix_v1.docx as starting point).
3) Ben: finalize sensitivity tables for legal to reference in the appendix.
4) Karthik/Finance: prepare fallback credit schedule in case vendor prices fall (rebate language).

If Marissa signs off (cc’d), we can present this to Atlas procurement and target legal redlines by Dec 6 as requested. I’ll pre-authorize finance to accept the 12% cap.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Finance — Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: approval_matrix_v1.docx (internal approval matrix)
